decisive_spans.text: Revealed a patent foramen ovale measuring 7.34 mm in width with a continuous, pure right-to-left shunt on colour flow mapping

response.rationale: The patient's history of progressive cyanosis, recurrent chest pain and shortness of breath, along with echocardiographic evidence of a right-to-left shunt through a patent foramen ovale, strongly supports Eisenmenger Syndrome. The enlarged hilar shadow and widened pulmonary arteries further support this diagnosis. While D3 (Congenital heart disease with shunt reversal) is also supported by the patent foramen ovale with right-to-left shunt, Eisenmenger Syndrome specifically describes the severe pulmonary hypertension and shunt reversal that has occurred in this patient, making it a more precise diagnosis. D2 and D4 are contradicted by the absence of pulmonary embolism or arteriovenous fistulae.
